dc70b0.surface: API staff routes (staff/index.ts): reservation, guest, venue settings actions
dc70b0.risk_area: Role authorization, venue scoping, IDOR, mass assignment
dc70b0.evidence: Static review found requireAuth plus venue access/role checks at affected staff handlers; reservation edits build an explicit update field map rather than passing arbitrary request properties to Prisma. Live unauthenticated checks to /staff/day return 401.

601cbc.risk_area: Role authorization, cross-venue IDOR, mass assignment
601cbc.evidence: Read requires authentication, venue access and admin role; layout mutation also enforces venue-admin role and validates referenced areas/tables against target venue. Image mutation requires isSuperAdmin. Live unauthenticated GET returned 401.

0156ce.surface: API public reservation and venue routes
0156ce.risk_area: IDOR and mass assignment / privilege boundary
0156ce.evidence: Public booking schema constrains source to guest-claimable marketing channels and handler explicitly maps fields, deriving venue from slug; selected seating area and table are checked against that venue. Public reservation retrieval returns limited booking summary by booking code. No cross-venue request proof of unauthorized disclosure was found in reviewed route paths.

0b28e4.evidence: Reviewed all Prisma filters and raw SQL in reservation creation; every raw value uses tagged-template interpolation with UUID casts and no unsafe query APIs. Live slug/table/area payloads containing SQL metacharacters were treated as values and did not alter query behavior.

7dd28b.evidence: Prisma findUnique/findMany predicates use typed value fields; raw SQL helper queries use tagged-template parameter interpolation. Live slug metacharacters returned not-found, and malformed dates produced validation/runtime errors without query syntax execution.

55a2df.surface: Changed API route query construction (staff routes, tables, settings)
55a2df.risk_area: SQL/NoSQL/command injection via where/orderBy or raw query inputs
55a2df.evidence: Searched route/library sources for Prisma raw query APIs and dynamic filters. Raw SQL is limited to tagged-template queries with parameterized values; request-derived Prisma filters are fixed-shape and no user-controlled orderBy/query structure or command execution exists.

2b0273.risk_area: credentialed cross-origin access and CSRF Origin enforcement
2b0273.evidence: Live API is reachable. Current helper allows credentialed CORS only for exact configured origins; unset allowlist disables cross-origin access. Unsafe methods with a supplied Origin outside the allowlist are rejected before route processing. Target runtime allowlist/credentialed browser cross-origin impact remains conditional on deployment configuration.

73a222.evidence: Handler serializes capacity checks by locking all bookable seating-area rows (pickAreaForParty) or the chosen area row (FOR UPDATE) before summing active reservations and inserting. The live venue/availability endpoints responded, but I did not create bookings because the live mutation is durable; no bypass was observed in the source path.

981857.risk_area: CSV formula injection across exported fields
981857.evidence: Both export handlers apply csvEscape to every emitted cell, and the helper prefixes a single quote when a value begins with optional whitespace then =, +, -, or @; it also handles initial tab/CR. Live authenticated export validation was blocked because seeded login credentials were unavailable.

f01c7f.evidence: Codes are generated from 8 random bytes into an eight-character 32-symbol alphabet (40 bits); the GET and cancellation routes have no route-level rate limit or code-format restriction. Twelve invalid-code GETs returned 404 without throttling, but no valid reservation code was available to measure practical enumeration or confirm impact.

8e7c23.risk_area: live authenticated CSV formula injection validation
8e7c23.evidence: No seeded credentials could be obtained from available mounted seed data, so emitted CSV rows could not be exercised live; static code shows all output cells use csvEscape, but runtime bypass behavior against deployed route remains unconfirmed.

f0f5de.risk_area: Feedback state machine and unauthenticated abuse
f0f5de.evidence: Handler requires reservation status completed and enforces one feedback row with a database-unique reservationId; however, no valid completed code was available and the test did not exercise feedback mutation or concurrent submissions. Rating/comments/tags schema lacks bounds, though Fastify's global body limit constrains request size; exact stored-data impact remains unverified.

105c25.risk_area: Authentication, session cookies, brute-force controls, password reset/invite
105c25.evidence: Live probes showed /staff/login rejects invalid credentials and /staff/me returns 401 without a session. Source shows HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite=Lax session cookies and an in-memory 10-failure limiter; however the mounted checkout has no Git metadata, so changed hunks versus the specified merge base could not be established, and reset/invite flows were not found in this API.

8b00f4.evidence: Public create/cancel/feedback routes use no ambient authenticated browser session; they rely on reservation creation input or booking code as bearer capability. This makes classic cookie-based CSRF inapplicable; no demonstrated cross-origin path to a valid booking code was found.

e7f411.surface: API secrets exposure via runtime configuration and repository public assets
e7f411.evidence: Reviewed API entrypoint, settings mapper, and source references; these do not directly return environment secrets, and /health only returned status. Full diff provenance could not be verified because the mounted checkout lacks Git metadata; no credential-bearing endpoint or reset/invite flow was identified in this slice.

b3ca9a.risk_area: host-based auth/routing bypass and header trust
b3ca9a.evidence: Tested Host/X-Forwarded-Host routing across book.gioigroup.com, gioigroup.com, localhost and preview hosts; book host blocks staff paths (404), while API endpoints still return 401 without session. No privilege bypass demonstrated.

ca3090.surface: Nuxt dev asset endpoints on http://host.docker.internal:3002 (/_nuxt/@fs, /_nuxt/@vite/client, source maps)
ca3090.evidence: Unauthenticated GET /_nuxt/@fs/Users/heyrcg/Documents/Works/gioi/apps/web/nuxt.config.ts returned 200 JavaScript containing source; /_nuxt/@vite/client returned 200 (179896 bytes) and /_nuxt/@fs/etc/passwd was blocked 403. The configured devServer host is not an effective production boundary when this service runs Nuxt dev.

d5401c.risk_area: authentication redirect and function-level authorization bypass
d5401c.evidence: Login next parameter is constrained to a single-origin path via /^\/(?![/\\])/, and auth/admin middleware fetches /staff/me then gates admin pages by role; unauthenticated live requests to API staff/admin routes returned 401.

499ae2.risk_area: client-side IDOR/cross-venue access and auth session handling
499ae2.evidence: Client sends venue and object IDs directly to API; server-side authorization could not be fully verified without seeded staff credentials. API rejects unauthenticated calls, but cross-venue enforcement remains a backend question.

795474.risk_area: schema/migration security and sensitive field exposure
795474.evidence: Reviewed added reservation/table, venue grace, and notice migrations plus changed schema/generated models; changes add relational fields and operational settings only, with no credentials, permissive auth metadata, or secret-bearing columns.

0afe8c.evidence: Workspace checkout contains no .claude/report build files listed in inherited diff context; inspected available docs/config references and found no newly introduced executable shelling or embedded credentials in reviewable files.

9f8045.risk_area: SSRF, host-header confusion, path normalization, open redirect
9f8045.evidence: Reviewed host-derived routing and live-tested Host/X-Forwarded-Host variants, encoded CRLF, query/path normalization, and cross-host booking routes. Redirect target is fixed runtime bookUrl; no attacker-controlled URL or server-side fetch is exposed.

c8dd03.risk_area: XML/Markdown injection, SSRF, cache poisoning, secret disclosure
c8dd03.evidence: Routes interpolate operator-configured site/book URLs and static VENUE_SEO data only; no request-controlled input or outbound fetch. Live responses returned fixed URLs and proper content types.

a9916c.risk_area: SSRF, proxy path traversal, header forwarding, cache poisoning
a9916c.evidence: Inspected fixed-destination PostHog and API rewrites; live-tested /ingest and /api path variants including double slashes, URL-like segments, traversal normalization, and trailing slash. Destinations are compile-time fixed and no user-controlled upstream URL is accepted.

65bd0b.surface: Web server SEO routes and host routing
65bd0b.risk_area: open redirect, host-header routing confusion, XML injection
65bd0b.evidence: Reviewed changed host middleware, sitemap.xml, llms.txt, and vercel routing; redirect destinations are runtime-configured first-party book/site URLs, sitemap/llms values derive static VENUE_SEO and configured URLs, with no attacker-controlled persistence reaching these sinks.

0a7ba0.risk_area: secret leakage and unsafe deployment configuration
0a7ba0.evidence: Reviewed changed vercel config, Nuxt config references, static assets and SEO utilities; no embedded credentials or attacker-controlled command execution was introduced. CSP and security headers are present in deployment config.

0bc461.surface: Nuxt dev asset/source serving on http://host.docker.internal:3002
0bc461.evidence: Live GET /_nuxt/Users/heyrcg/Documents/Works/gioi/apps/web/nuxt.config.ts and app.vue returned 200 JavaScript/source with absolute workstation paths; root HTML references /_nuxt/@vite/client. Captured requests 113 and 125.

fa233b.evidence: Unauthenticated requests returned 200 transformed `nuxt.config.ts` and `app.vue` source plus Vite HMR code; Vite blocked only paths outside its allow-list. Filed as `vuln-0001`.

0af21d.surface: Admin floor-plan image upload and public SVG rendering
0af21d.evidence: Changed API restricts image to data:image SVG/PNG/JPEG/WebP base64 with 4 MB character/body limits and admin auth; frontend renders as SVG <image> under CSP img-src self/data/blob, so active SVG script execution was not demonstrated.

1638f9.surface: Web/API dependency manifests and runtime output (.output/public)
1638f9.risk_area: known vulnerable dependencies and secret exposure
1638f9.evidence: No lockfiles present in /workspace/web or /workspace/api; package manifests contain no credentials. Scanned public/.output/.data for secret markers without hits. Runtime output did expose dev source, tracked separately.

9fedb6.evidence: Live probes with quote/boolean-style slug payloads returned normal 404s; Prisma where clauses are parameterized. Public venue response is an explicit allowlist and availability returns only slot metadata.

f3ebcc.evidence: All raw SQL uses tagged Prisma parameters; creation and public lookup responses explicitly return booking code/status or summary only, not guest/internal fields, hashes, idempotency keys, or session data.

5e2b68.risk_area: Prisma query injection / over-broad guest or user data exposure
5e2b68.evidence: Search found no unsafeRaw APIs or request-controlled orderBy; staff responses map selected guest/reservation fields explicitly. Full guest/reservation records are only queried after requireAuth plus venue access checks.

dbf3f2.surface: Admin venue/settings, analytics, audit, CSV routes
dbf3f2.risk_area: Sensitive hashes/tokens and unsafe dynamic filters
dbf3f2.evidence: Admin venue/settings and analytics are behind requireAuth and venue/admin checks; user listing maps fields without passwordHash, audit actorUser is mapped without hash, and CSV/analytics use fixed Prisma filters and bounded limit.

89716f.surface: Raw SQL capacity/status queries in public reservations and staff routes
89716f.evidence: Every $queryRaw/$executeRaw call is tagged-template Prisma SQL with interpolated values bound as parameters; enum casts and UUID casts occur inside SQL and no unsafe/raw string API is used.

c675ab.surface: Nuxt venue pages and SEO head generation
c675ab.evidence: Confirmed complete source path: authenticated admin PATCH accepts arbitrary Venue.address/mapsUrl; public venue data feeds useVenueSeo; JSON.stringify output is assigned to script innerHTML without escaping `<`, so a `</script><script>` payload can terminate JSON-LD. Live API accepted and returned the payload, but deployed web runtime used a separate upstream dataset, preventing browser execution against the same record during this run.

49e5e2.surface: Venue maps links in pages/[venue]/index.vue and confirmation page
49e5e2.risk_area: Stored XSS via javascript: URL in href
49e5e2.evidence: Venue PATCH endpoint accepts mapsUrl as arbitrary string and pages bind info.mapsUrl directly to href. A javascript: scheme would execute on visitor click; live API write path was verified, but separate upstream web runtime prevented end-to-end browser execution in this run.

a777d8.surface: FloorPlanSvg image href and static SEO sitemap/llms routes
a777d8.risk_area: DOM XSS / HTML or XML injection
a777d8.evidence: Floor-plan image is rendered as SVG image href (scripts do not execute in image context); sitemap and llms values derive from static VENUE_SEO and operator runtime siteUrl, not attacker-controlled request data.
